subject: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria (Acme Retail)

Hi Javier / Sophie —

Thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC started: 

1) Success criteria (what Acme needs to consider the trial successful):
   - Quality: >= 85% pass rate on the evaluation prompt set (50 representative prompts across your use cases)
   - Latency: p50 generation < 500ms for 256-token responses (target for UX flows)
   - Multilingual coverage: Spanish and Portuguese must have parity with English for key intents (no more than 10% drop in pass rate)
   - Reliability: <= 2% error rate and stable throughput for peak test load (simulate 50 concurrent users)

2) Model selection (initial recommendation for the trial):
   - Primary: Llama 2 13B Chat (quantized 4-bit) — best balance of multilingual quality and cost for your conversational use cases
   - Latency-first option: Mistral Instruct 7B — lower latency and cost; good fallback for high throughput paths
   - Fallback: Llama 2 7B (ultra-cost-efficient) — route non-critical/background requests here if we need to cap cost

Notes on multilingual needs: both Llama 2 13B and Mistral 7B have reasonably good Spanish/Portuguese performance out of the box; we'll run targeted prompt-tests during week 1 of the POC and share a language-specific pass/fail matrix.

3) Evaluation plan & ownership:
   - Acme: provide a canonical prompt set (50 prompts) + 200 anonymized in-domain examples for scoring (Javier / Sophie)
   - Redwood: provide test harness, data ingestion script, and evaluation metrics dashboard (Marissa will own setup)
   - Timeline: get dataset by Thu 3/5 -> run baseline tests Fri 3/6 -> share initial results Mon 3/9 -> iterate Wed 3/11

4) Next steps / asks from Acme:
   - Share the prompt set and the example payloads (upload to the Drive link below)
   - Confirm whether we should prioritize latency vs. raw quality for the initial run (we recommended quality first)

Attachments: Acme_PO_Criteria.xlsx (upload expected)

I'll loop Marissa in to propose the exact infra and test harness details. Happy to hop on a quick 30m to align if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the biz team will sign off on quality thresholds, but they're likely to be more prescriptive; I'll share the formal rubric by end of day 3/4 (see attached Acme_PO_Criteria.xlsx).
- Multilingual: Spanish is critical; Portuguese is "nice-to-have" but would be great to include. If there's a significant quality gap we'd need a plan to route Portuguese queries differently.
- Timeline: procurement needs to review any trial connectivity/terms. Can Redwood provide a short (1-pager) POC SOW and an example network diagram we can send to procurement?

Also cc'd Sophie (technical lead) — Sophie, can you confirm the sample data format (JSONL or CSV) and whether any PII will be included? We will sanitize most data but may include masked tokens for context.

Hi Javier / Sophie —

Marissa here (Solutions Engineer) — quick note on the evaluation plan and technical setup: 

1) Data / format: we prefer JSONL for prompt+response pairs (one JSON per line). If you have CSV we can convert but please include a column for language tag. Masked PII is fine. 

2) Test harness & metrics:
   - Redwood will run the baseline tests against the three model variants (Llama2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B-instruct, Llama2-7B) and produce:
     * Pass rate per-prompt (binary pass/fail based on rubric)
     * Language parity delta (EN vs ES/PT)
     * Latency p50/p95 and tokens/sec throughput
     * Resource & cost estimate per-100k requests

3) Infra & access:
   - We'll provide a temporary trial API key scoped to the POC, and a short POC SOW 1-pager + network diagram (attaching the POC setup guide).
   - For Spanish-heavy tests we can enable a higher-quality config (slightly higher memory/compute) for the first run.

4) Fallback routing plan:
   - Primary: Llama2-13B (quality); fallback to Mistral-7B on load or cost triggers; route background batch jobs to Llama2-7B. We'll instrument routing thresholds in the dashboard so Acme can tune them.

5) Timeline (proposed):
   - 3/05: Redwood share SOW + setup guide (done)
   - 3/06: Acme uploads prompt set + sample examples to Drive
   - 3/09: Redwood runs baseline & shares initial dashboard
   - 3/11: Joint review to decide next model tuning/quantization choices

Attachments: redwood-poc-setup-guide.pdf (contains example network diagram and SOW 1-pager)

If that looks good I'll stand up the trial key and the test harness this week.

Cheers,
